text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak visits Kuwait for Middle East peace talks.
- Liberation from expats. The government plans to gradually replace foreigners in the public sector with Kuwaiti employees.
- MPs hit dependency on oil revenue, making Kuwait's future hostage to oil prices. Parliament met on Saturday to discuss the government's economic policies.
- Salaries, wages and benefits account for 50 percent of the government's expenses, a leading economist said. The welfare state employes more than 90 of Kuwaitis in the workforce.
- United Arab Emirates education official arrives for three-day visit.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange sets new records in Saturday trading. The index rose 40.9 points to 2,2338.2.
- Representatives of 13 British companies to visit Kuwait on April 29 to boost trade between the two countries.

- Saudi Arabian King Fahd holds talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak amid expectations to hold a full or a mini-Arab summit. Mubarak on Friday said he was against holding a full summit at the time being.
- Thirty firms participate in travel and tourism fair in Kuwait.
